item: a committing restore refuses while a registered background job that writes to the corpus runs, naming it (R659, OPEN_QUEUE item 21 option B reduced); item 18 closed as a stated limit with a guard (R660)
summary: BEFORE: the restore's exclusive window stopped only the collection loop and Run now; a registered background job that commits to the corpus (the governments loads, tag backfills, language detection, source qualification, the mailbox pull...) kept writing, and everything it committed between the working copy and the swap was discarded by the swap, silently. The task manager's 'another job is writing' ask read a second, hand-kept list (_DB_WRITER_KINDS) that missed 9 of 13 writer kinds. NOW: running_writer_jobs() in src/jobs/background.py reads the registry's own is_writer flags (one list); run_restore(commit=True) raises RestoreRefused naming the running writers by label, before it prepares anything and again at the working copy, with nothing imported and nothing written; a preview is never refused. A job that stops itself inside the exclusive window (the new yields_to_exclusive flag, set only on reindex-resume, whose worker stops in its article loop and which the import queue restarts after every item) is not named while the window is open, so a queued import does not refuse its own second item. The ask (db_writers_busy/busy_with) now joins the hand-kept kinds with every registry writer. The refusal is a fixed English sentence the page turns into the operator's language (ooServerText, the job labels translated where the page has them), keyed in all 12 locales. tests/test_restore_refuses_writer_jobs.py (6 tests, red on main: the function, the flag and the refusal did not exist). R660: OPEN_QUEUE item 18 / R338 R340 closes as the stated limit written in tests/test_repair_probe_parked_writer.py's docstring, and test_every_raw_write_lock_transaction_in_src_is_classified pins every BEGIN IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE a statement in src/ issues (6 files, 16 statements, each with why it cannot hold SQLite's lock across the repair's window), so a later ungated writer fails that test. Stated limits: a job started after the working copy is not caught; writers that are not registry jobs (the collection pass, the housekeeping lane, the Wikipedia drain, API write routes, the newsletter and source deletions) and writers left unflagged on purpose (ai-coordinator, tests/test_job_writer_flags.py) are outside the list. Release-notes line: «An import now refuses to start while a background job is writing to your corpus, and names the job, instead of silently discarding what that job writes during the import.»
